enable.name: Throttle Failsafe Enable
enable.description: The throttle failsafe allows you to configure a software failsafe activated by a setting on the throttle input channel

options.label: Enabled Continue with Mission in Auto Mode (Removed in 4.0+)

value.name: Throttle Failsafe Value
value.description: The PWM level in microseconds on channel 3 below which throttle failsafe triggers

options.name: Failsafe options bitmask
options.description: Bitmask of additional options for battery, radio, & GCS failsafes. 0 disables all options.

bits.label: Continue if in Auto on RC failsafe
Continue if in Auto on GCS failsafe
Continue if in Guided on RC failsafe
Continue if landing on any failsafe
Continue if in pilot controlled modes on GCS failsafe

field.name: Ground Station Failsafe Enable
field.description: Controls whether failsafe will be invoked (and what action to take) when connection with Ground station is lost for at least 5 seconds. See FS_OPTIONS param for additional actions, or for cases allowing Mission continuation, when GCS failsafe is enabled.

options.label: RTL or Continue with Mission in Auto Mode (Removed in 4.0+-see FS_OPTIONS)

alt.name: RTL Altitude
alt.description: The minimum alt above home the vehicle will climb to before returning. If the vehicle is flying higher than this value it will return at its current altitude.

loitTime.name: RTL loiter time
loitTime.description: Time (in milliseconds) to loiter above home before beginning final descent

altFinal.name: RTL Final Altitude
altFinal.description: Altitude the vehicle will move to as the final stage of Returning to Launch or after completing a mission. Set to zero to land.

extra.name: RTL cone slope
extra.description: Defines a cone above home which determines maximum climb

extra.name: RTL minimum climb
extra.description: The vehicle will climb this many meters during the initial climb portion of the RTL

extra.name: RTL speed
extra.description: The speed in m/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain horizontally while flying home. If this is set to zero, WP_SPD will be used instead.

arming.note: This firmware splits arming checks into ARMING_* parameters (listed under Advanced Safety Parameters).

params.name: EKF Failsafe Action
params.description: Controls the action that will be taken when an EKF failsafe is invoked

params.name: EKF failsafe variance threshold
params.description: Allows setting the maximum acceptable compass, velocity, position and height variances. Used in arming check and EKF failsafe.

params.name: Crash check enable
params.description: This enables automatic crash checking. When enabled the motors will disarm if a crash is detected.

params.name: Vibration Failsafe enable
params.description: This enables the vibration failsafe which will use modified altitude estimation and control during high vibrations

params.name: RTL cone slope
params.description: Defines a cone above home which determines maximum climb

params.name: RTL minimum climb
params.description: The vehicle will climb this many meters during the initial climb portion of the RTL

params.name: RTL speed
params.description: The speed in m/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain horizontally while flying home. If this is set to zero, WP_SPD will be used instead.

params.name: Accelerometer error threshold
params.description: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.

params.name: Disable CrashDump Arming check
params.description: Must have value "1" if crashdump data is present on the system, or a prearm failure will be raised.  Do not set this parameter unless the risks of doing so are fully understood.  The presence of a crash dump means that the firmware currently installed has suffered a critical software failure which resulted in the autopilot immediately rebooting.  The crashdump file gives diagnostic information which can help in finding the issue, please contact the ArduPIlot support team.  If this crashdump data is present, the vehicle is likely unsafe to fly.  Check the ArduPilot documentation for more details.

params.name: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model
params.description: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model.  X and y axis are compared using this threhold, Z axis uses 2x this threshold.  0 to disable check

params.name: Required mission items
params.description: Bitmask of mission items that are required to be planned in order to arm the aircraft

params.name: Require vehicle location
params.description: Require that the vehicle have an absolute position before it arms.  This can help ensure that the vehicle can Return To Launch.

params.name: Arming options
params.description: Options that can be applied to change arming behaviour

params.name: Arming with Rudder enable/disable
params.description: Allow arm/disarm by rudder input. When enabled arming can be done with right rudder, disarming with left rudder. Rudder arming only works with throttle at zero +- deadzone (RCx_DZ). Depending on vehicle type, arming in certain modes is prevented. See the wiki for each vehicle. Caution is recommended when arming if it is allowed in an auto-throttle mode!

params.name: Arm Checks to Skip (bitmask)
params.description: Checks to skip prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks before allowing arming that will be skipped. For most users it is recommended to leave this at the default of 0 (no checks skipped). In extreme circumstances, a value of -1 can be used to skip all non-mandatory current and future checks.

params.name: Yaw behaviour during missions
params.description: Determines how the autopilot controls the yaw during missions and RTL
